- **Positions — packaged, role-compatible agent presets, and the host trust root that governs them (bob#195 slice 1).** A new packaged `positions/` directory ships two first-party presets, `builder` and `reviewer`, each naming an existing role (it never carries or edits one) and declaring the tools it requests, the capabilities it permits (and which are on by default), and the packaged files it uses (a seed soul; skill, prompt and threshold files are later slices, and a manifest that declares one is refused until it loads). Three commands land: `bob hire <name> --as <position>` (scaffold a NEW agent, ratify the host grant, store the diff baseline, initialize the override repository, and run the existing hiring interview, which keeps the agent's own identity in its seed soul — the identity header plus the position's persona, not the generic packaged soul alone), `bob position adopt <name> --as <position>` (bind an EXISTING agent without rewriting it — it independently resolves the agent before and after binding, REQUIRES the two effective configurations to be equal or refuses, verifies its requests against the position, role and new grant, records the binding, ratification and normalized baseline, initializes the override repository, and leaves the pre-existing `bob.yaml` and `soul.md` byte-for-byte unchanged), and `bob position diff <name>` (the ratified baseline against the current effective configuration, comparing role, tools, tool exclusions, the residency decision, the resident-shell grant, capabilities, resolved files and the soul). A **host grant** ratifies the role name, the position name/version/hash, the maximum tool set and the maximum capability set. The grant file is stored under the host state root, but that placement is NOT a containment boundary — any same-user writer, including the agent's own built-in file tools, can edit it — so what it gives is boot checks, not authentication: Boot checks a grant against the packaged position selected by that grant and its role; it refuses a previously bound agent with a missing or unreadable grant, but it does not authenticate the grant or detect every same-user edit. Isolation from same-user writes is deferred to bob#189. Every boot loads the current packaged role, compares the manifest name/version/hash/role against the grant, AND compares the grant's frozen agent, tool set, capability set and resident-shell flag against the booted agent, the selected manifest's sets and the packaged role's flag, refusing each mismatch by field (the field, the grant value, the packaged value and the remedy); it refuses BY NAME each tool or capability outside the grant maxima BEFORE any intersection, then applies the narrow-only local disables, then passes the narrowed tools to `resolveToolPolicy`, which enforces the packaged role's ceiling, and the narrowed capabilities to `resolveCapabilities`, and it passes the PACKAGED role's resident-shell flag — never the grant's — into tool-policy resolution. A **position** is data, never a trust root. The local `overrides/` layer is a per-agent Git repository that may only SUBTRACT — named, schema-checked disable lists for tools and capabilities, and allow-listed files that replace a packaged position file at the same relative path (the soul is NOT overridable); every other key (an `enable:` key, a top-level `tools:` key, providers, secrets, comms) is refused by name. The DECLARED file list and the files PRESENT under `overrides/files/` (symlink entries included) are each checked against the manifest allow-list AND must agree, so a present-but-undeclared file, an unlisted symlink entry and a declared-but-absent file are each refused by name; every override read is realpath-confined. Slice 1 ships NO host secret bindings: a position that declares a secret is refused at hire and adoption. The effective-config resolver routes through EVERY session entry path — one-shot `bob run`, the persistent runtime, `bob launch`, `bob onboard` and `bob align` — and an adopted agent's setup sessions run the fixed setup policy, exactly `read` + `write_soul`, like every other agent's (bob#204; never the grant's own tools). An agent with no grant is not adopted, so every existing `bob init` agent keeps booting unchanged — the one exception is the binding marker: a previously bound agent whose marker directory entry is present but whose grant is missing refuses to boot rather than falling back. Slice 1 loads only positions under bob's own packaged `positions/` directory (bare name or the confined `path:<name>` form); host secret bindings, skill/prompt/threshold files, arbitrary `path:`/`npm:`/`git:` sources, position upgrade, the model selector, the performance review, full jarvis and new comms are later slices. (`test/shell/positions-195.test.ts`)
